description:
Overview

The Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights opened admissions on 17 November 2026 for its September 2027 LLM in International Crimes, Justice and Human Rights. A limited number of full scholarships are available, covering tuition fees and living expenses in Geneva for 10 months.

This is an exceptional opportunity for law graduates and human-rights practitioners who want to build a career in international criminal justice, transitional justice or human-rights law. Scholarships are highly competitive and allocated using donor criteria including academic merit, financial need, extracurricular achievements, country of study and country of residence.

The programme is a one-year, full-time, in-person LLM–MAS (60 ECTS) with a strong focus on accountability for international crimes and serious human-rights violations, and on victims’ rights.

Funding and Duration

Geneva Academy full scholarship coverage
ItemDetails
Scholarship typeFull scholarship — limited number, highly competitive.
Tuition feesFully covered (the published LLM–MAS tuition is CHF 18,000).
Living expensesCovered in Geneva for 10 months.
AirfareNot expressly included in the published coverage — plan your own travel budget.
DurationOne-year LLM programme, starting September 2027.
Selection criteriaAcademic merit, financial need, extracurricular achievements, and donor criteria (country of study/residence).

Eligibility

Admission and scholarship requirements
ItemDetails
DegreeA full law degree that qualifies you to sit the bar exam in your country. Candidates from other disciplines may be considered case by case with relevant professional experience and university-level international-law study. You may apply in your final year if you will have your diploma by June 2027.
English proficiencyC1 level, shown through a recognised test. Exemptions apply if English is your mother tongue, you completed a degree taught in English, or you have two or more years of academic or professional experience in an English-speaking environment.
NationalityScholarships are only available to citizens of eligible non-Western countries — the official Geneva Academy page holds the full eligible-country list (commonly the OECD DAC list). Confirm your country is eligible before applying.
DocumentsTwo signed recommendation letters on letterhead (at least one academic), plus the career-plan and awards/grants forms from the application guidelines — the application cannot be submitted without them.

Application Dates

Key dates for the September 2027 intake
ItemDetails
Applications open17 November 2026.
Scholarship application deadline17 January 2027 — apply on the scholarship track before this date.
Regular (non-scholarship) deadline17 February 2027.
Programme startSeptember 2027.
Admission feeA non-refundable CHF 100 admission fee is due within one week of submitting, and applies to scholarship applicants too. Applications are not reviewed until it is paid.
Review processApplications are reviewed on a rolling basis — apply early.

How to Apply

  • Open the Geneva Academy LLM programme page and read the LLM–MAS application guidelines carefully.
  • Create or log in with a SWITCH edu-ID, then apply online for the LLM in International Crimes, Justice and Human Rights on the scholarship track.
  • Upload the required documents: law degree or equivalent, transcripts, English C1 proof (or exemption), CV, motivation letter, two signed recommendation letters, and the completed career-plan and awards forms.
  • Pay the non-refundable CHF 100 admission fee within one week of submission, and submit before 17 January 2027 for scholarship consideration.
  • Confirm your nationality is on the eligible non-Western country list before applying.

Official Link

Geneva Academy — LLM in International Crimes, Justice and Human Rights

Important Notes

  • Airfare is not expressly included in the published scholarship coverage — budget for travel separately.
  • Only citizens of eligible non-Western countries can receive the scholarship.
  • The CHF 100 admission fee applies even to scholarship applicants, and the application is not reviewed until it is paid.
  • Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis — apply early.
